english: Life has seasons
The eye of God is big (large)
The words of the elders are blessed
We start by being foolish and we eventually become wise
swahili: Tunaanza kwa kuwa wajinga na hatimaye tunakuwa wenye hekima

english: The neck cannot become the head
A proverb does not answer itself
note: It is easier to see someone else's evil than it is to see one's own.

english: Even that which is despised can triumph
A falling tree will cause others to fall

maasai: Iyiolo ake eningua kake imiyiola eniloto
english: You know where you come from but you don't know where you are going
One finger does not (cannot) kill a louse
The stomach cannot steal and if it did, it would show itself
swahili: Tumbo haliwezi kuiba na kama lingeiba lingejionyesha lenyewe

english: Don't fight a lion with a stick
You will not be punished when you think before acting
swahili: Hutaadhibiwa ikiwa unafikiri kabla ya kutenda

english: Events follow one another like days
Life and death are not the same
note: Jesus went through and suffered on our behalf. He was raised to life (1Peter 3:18)

english: Home is not far away when you are alive

maasai: Iyiolo ake enigua kake imiyiola enilo
english: Be as familiar with observation as you are with the place you live
swahili: Fahamu uchunguzi kama vile unavyofahamu mahali unapoishi

english: In life the assured time of good life if today, tomorrow might be a different story
Pans (pancakes) take shift on fire
Sometimes you have, other times you don't have
The child may see thieves before the father does

maasai: Eikasha aisinanisho nibikoo along karsisisho nie irakiti
english: It is better to be poor and live long than rich and die young

maasai: Ainyoo pee iton enaa enkitok nayamishe?
english: Why do you behave like a woman whose son has just married?
God, shield me with your wings (Prayer)
A new idea follows an old one
Don't reply one wrong with another
A person does not itch from a thorn that is not his
The elephant does not get tired of his tusks
note: Despite our sinfulness, God is with us all the time

english: There is no poverty of a single day
interpretation: Readiness for God means that we are prepared to do the smallest things or the largest things – to make a difference.

english: One head cannot contain all knowledge
You cannot force water up a hill
interpretation: it's not possible to do the impossible. You cannot serve two masters. You cannot serve God and devil. You will only be able to serve one

maasai: Atejo apa oledukuya mongoi mpira Enkai niarr olaisimani
english: The elders said that lies go up and kills a robber
Alright! Is it so easy to say!
interpretation: Fear says, There is a lion in the way.

english: There is no friendship which is one way
interpretation: Friendship is mutual

english: The withered tree will destroy the healthy tree when it falls down
It is the belly which daily gives thanks
A lie cannot fill the palm
Trouble comes to those who look for it
Do not jump about, for there is no use in jumping about
Foolishness first, then wisdom

maasai: Iyiolo ake enijo kake miyiolo enikijokini
english: You only know what you say but you don't know what you will be told
Nobody can say he is settled anywhere forever: it is only the mountains which do not move from their places
The eye cannot penetrate darkness
The teeth do see poverty

maasai: Meeta empur nemejo nanu eedo kidong'oe
english: There is no lizard that does not claim to possess the longest tail
note: This is about boasting or showing off

english: The cow has no owner
note: According to Maasai myth cows are gift from God to Maasai as he (Maasai exclaimed; 'Ayie! Yie... Nkumok oleng – There are so many') 'Inkishu' – Cows are sent from heaven.

english: The tongue has no joint
interpretation: The tongue is flexible and can say anything. There is no control.

english: There is not such a thing in the world as a sheep of many colours
interpretation: You are either hot or cold; you cannot be both.

english: There is no one who has finished, there is only who is still at it
interpretation: we are all on the race, no one has finished

english: There is no one way friendship
interpretation: friendship is mutual

english: The boaster (the proud) will not cross the valley
interpretation: God rejects the proud

english: The neck does not go beyond the head
That which is Godly cannot be pushed away with the fore arm
One cane devour incredible loads of meat
Twenty sheep to him is just a taste
Ooh! This man is like a leaking gourd that cannot be filled
note: This proverb talks about a man who had a big appetite for meat. It is a warning not to be greedy.

english: Do not go to the plains without somebody to take the dust out of your eye
It is not possible to hold a walking stick as well as the stomach
The zebra cannot do away with its stripes
interpretation: One cannot give up one's habits that were developed in childhood

english: Cooking pots exchange places on the fire
interpretation: Things come at different times

english: Happiness is as good as food
interpretation: Good company can be better than good food

english: The children are the bright moon
interpretation: Take care of the little that you have

english: Do not show the hawk how to fly (Or do not show a wild hog a bow)
interpretation: Do not be over-confident of yourself. Take one step at a time

english: An elephant is not able to endure beating from many (Or an elephant fears attack from several sides)
interpretation: One man or a small group of men can attack many more

english: Even a brown he-goat cannot cleanse him
interpretation: it has gone beyond repair

english: Baboons (or certain animals) do not go far from the place of their birth
interpretation: A man never forgets his original home

english: One head cannot consume all knowledge
interpretation: There are others as wise as you, one needs advice from other people

english: It is not acquisition that is difficult, it is retention (Obtaining something is easier than looking after it properly)
interpretation: Take care of that which you have; a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush

maasai: Minkar orpashe lolokai ompaka niduaki kewan
english: Do not repair another man's fence until you have seen your own
interpretation: Help yourself first in order to be able to be of use to others

english: Eat a sweet until it becomes bitter (Or A mouth that has eaten a good thing will eat a bad one)
interpretation: Things change/life can change

english: My friend, you bring me evil (Or A constant complain can lead you to bad ways)
interpretation: A friend can bring you evil

maasai: Ore sininye esidai oneyado olgos nepi inkonyek, nemedol entaisere
english: Even the ostrich, with its long neck and sharp eyes, cannot see what will happen in the future
swahili: Hata mbuni, mwenye shingo ndefu na macho makali, hawezi kuona kitakachotokea wakati ujao
note: No one knows day or hour... Be prepared all the time

english: Facing backwards does not perform itself.
A blind sheep might chance across rain water.
swahili: Kondoo asiyeona anaweza kupata maji ya mvua kwa bahati.

english: The bad words coming from the mouth are worse than a fart.
swahili: Maneno mabaya kutoka mdomoni ni mabaya kuliko mshuzi.

english: A dog cannot guard two homes.
A zebra takes its stripes wherever it goes.
swahili: Punda milia hupeleka milia yake popote iendapo.

english: No one is wise that has been fooled (or lied to).
The nose can never lead.
He who has a father is still not circumcised (subordinate).
swahili: Yule aliye na baba bado hajatahiriwa.

english: Clever is the eye that has traveled (Experience is the best teacher).
swahili: Jicho lililosafiri ndilo lenye busara (Uzoefu ni mwalimu bora).

english: Life and death are not alike.
swahili: Uhai na kifo sio jambo moja.

maasai: Eoroo keon aitalam ilchoreta lenyenak enaa osikiria omwuoi
english: He separates himself from his friends like a sick donkey.
swahili: Anajitenga na marafiki zake kama punda mgonjwa.

english: I'm not a fool because I don't live in the same homestead as my in-law.
swahili: Mimi si mjinga kwa sababu sikaa kwenye boma moja na shemeji yangu.
note: Implies that close proximity can lead to conflict.

english: Perhaps you love him/her, yet you don't help him/her (Actions speak louder than words).
It cannot happen that you love him/her and you don't help him/her (Love must be demonstrated).
swahili: Haiwezi kutokea kwamba unampenda na humsaidii.

english: All things which their owners carefully tend last a long time.
swahili: Vitu vyote ambavyo wamiliki wao huvitunza kwa uangalifu hudumu kwa muda mrefu.

english: A zebra takes its stripes wherever it goes.
swahili: Punda milia hupeleka milia yake popote iendapo.
note: Similar to No. 77, emphasizing inescapable nature.

english: Don't force water up a hill.
Fire makes the cooking stick straight.
A white goat does not spoil (a herd).
They moved homes and the red one was born (The fire remains after the move).

maasai: Tamanai teidia alo oldoinyio matamanu tena nimikitumo aikata
english: Go round one side of the mountain while I go round the other side, but we shall never meet.
I have an ox who lives in the midst of enemies (The tongue).
swahili: Nina ng'ombe wangu anayeishi katikati ya maadui.

english: If the teeth were as clean, it would be difficult to eat sour milk.
swahili: Kama meno yangekuwa safi sana, ingekuwa vigumu kula maziwa ya siki.

english: The trouble is only for one day.
swahili: Shida ni ya siku moja tu.

english: A white goat does not bring a disaster.
When you talk, be like a sheep (soft and gentle).
Hunger makes the mind clear.
A homestead cannot refuse its inhabitants.
A stick does not reject the fire.
A child does not know what is beneficial.
The mouth makes the head shine (Your words reflect your character).
You cannot fight God nor refuse to pay debt.
swahili: Huwezi kupigana na Mungu wala kukataa kulipa deni.

english: A long-gone home cannot refuse its ox to graze.
swahili: Boma lililohama haliwezi kukataa ng’ombe wake kulisha.

english: The long-gone road is easy to return to.
swahili: Njia ya mbali ni rahisi kurudi.

english: A lion cannot be driven away with a stick.
It is the mouth that makes the head straight (Clear communication avoids trouble).
The stomach never forgets what it ate.
A cow is not finished while still being milked.
The ox follows the one who leads it.
God does not make a person born with two tongues (Cannot speak two truths).
swahili: Mungu hamzali mtu na ndimi mbili.

english: The one who eats alone keeps his mouth shut (Secrecy when eating is good).
The shield is worn on the field.
The cow makes the owner straight (Wealth gives confidence).
The ox of the women waits for the sick cow (Women's cattle are less valuable).
swahili: Ng’ombe wa wanawake husubiri ng’ombe mgonjwa.

english: Do not despise a shield because it is torn.
The hand that carries the shield is visible (Actions are seen).
The cow grazes at the homestead of the one who herds it.
swahili: Ng’ombe hula katika boma la yule anayemchunga.

english: Home is not far away when you are alive.
The mouth of the ox is the owner (The one who feeds you controls you).
The cattle of the man are many.
The broken shield is still visible.
You cannot hate a cow that gave you milk.
A cow knows the one who owns it.
One mouth sees (One person observes).
A cow cannot refuse to be tied in the homestead.
swahili: Ng’ombe hawezi kukataa kufungwa ndani ya boma.

english: The shield straightens the teeth (Danger compels discipline).
He who is successful never goes to waste.
The rich man has a cow.
The teeth of the one who has a cow never go to waste (You always have something to eat).
swahili: Meno ya aliye na ng'ombe haipotei.

english: The mouth makes the head straight.
The cow cannot lick itself (Need for external help).
The cow gives the owner a small piece of meat (A return on investment).
swahili: Ng’ombe humpa mmiliki kipande kidogo cha nyama.

english: The cow of the rich man cannot refuse its own teeth.
swahili: Ng’ombe wa tajiri hawezi kukataa meno yake.

english: The hand of the rich man sees the teeth (The rich are always well-fed).
The cow makes the owner honest.
A cow cannot refuse its teeth.
The successful man never wastes a piece of meat.
The cow waits for its teeth (The cow waits for its owner to eat).
The cow of the man does not lick its teeth (A man's worth is known).
swahili: Ng’ombe wa mwanamume hajilambi meno yake.

english: The cow cannot refuse the house it was born in.
The cow sees the meat of the rich man (The rich man shares his wealth).
The cow of the man is not far from home.
swahili: Ng’ombe wa mwanamume hayuko mbali na nyumbani.

english: The cow waits for the meat.
The teeth make the cow straight (Eating makes the cow healthy).
A cow does not lick meat (Focus on what is appropriate).
The cow licks its owner (Affection or recognition).
The rich man waits for the meat (His effort guarantees food).
The cow sees the home that is being built (The cow understands preparation).
The teeth cannot refuse the meat.
The owner makes the cow straight (The owner takes care of the cow).
The teeth give the cow meat.
The cow makes the rich man's teeth straight (The cow sustains him).
swahili: Ng'ombe hufanya meno ya tajiri kuwa sawa.

english: The cow of the man is not finished (A man’s resources are lasting).
The meat waits for the cow to have teeth.
swahili: Nyama inasubiri ng'ombe awe na meno.

english: The teeth lick the cow's meat (Eating is enjoyable).
The rich man’s meat is not finished.
The cow makes the owner’s meat straight.
The cow’s meat is not far away.
The cow of the rich man licks the meat.
The rich man cannot refuse his teeth.
The teeth make the rich man straight.
The cow sees its owner.
The teeth of the rich man are not finished.
The cow waits for its teeth at home.
The rich man licks the meat.
The cow of the man cannot refuse its teeth.
swahili: Ng’ombe wa mwanamume hawezi kukataa meno yake.

english: The owner makes the teeth straight (The owner ensures sustenance).
The teeth give the cow meat.
The rich man’s meat is not far away.
The cow sees the teeth of the rich man.
The cow's meat of the owner is not finished.
swahili: Nyama ya ng'ombe ya mmiliki haiishi.

english: The teeth of the rich man wait for the cow.
The cow of the man licks the meat's teeth.
swahili: Ng’ombe wa mwanamume hulamba meno ya nyama.

english: The rich man cannot refuse meat to have teeth.
swahili: Tajiri hawezi kukataa nyama ili awe na meno.

english: The teeth make the cow's meat straight (Easy to eat).
swahili: Meno hufanya nyama ya ng'ombe kuwa sawa.

english: The meat sees the cow of the owner.
The cow's teeth meat is not far away.
swahili: Nyama ya meno ya ng’ombe si mbali.

english: The owner waits for the teeth of the cow.
The teeth of the rich man lick the cow.
The cow cannot refuse meat to have an owner.
swahili: Ng’ombe hawezi kukataa nyama ili awe na mmiliki.

english: The rich man makes the cow's teeth straight.
swahili: Tajiri hufanya meno ya ng’ombe kuwa sawa.

english: The teeth see the cow’s meat.
The meat of the man’s cow is not far away.
swahili: Nyama ya ng’ombe ya mwanamume si mbali.

english: The cow waits for the rich man’s meat.
The meat licks the cow’s teeth.
The owner cannot refuse the rich man’s meat.
swahili: Mmiliki hawezi kukataa nyama ya tajiri.

english: The rich man makes the teeth’s meat straight.
swahili: Tajiri hufanya nyama ya meno kuwa sawa.

english: The man’s cow sees the meat’s teeth.
swahili: Ng’ombe ya mwanamume huona meno ya nyama.

english: The teeth's meat of the cow is not far away.
swahili: Nyama ya meno ya ng’ombe si mbali.

english: The rich man’s meat waits for the cow.
The owner licks the meat’s teeth.
The teeth cannot refuse the cow’s meat.
swahili: Meno hayawezi kukataa nyama ya ng’ombe.

english: The cow makes the rich man’s meat straight.
swahili: Ng’ombe hufanya nyama ya tajiri kuwa sawa.

english: The meat sees the teeth of the rich man.
The rich man’s meat’s teeth are not far away.
swahili: Meno ya nyama ya tajiri si mbali.

english: The meat’s teeth wait for the owner.
The cow licks the rich man’s meat.
The owner cannot refuse the meat’s teeth.
swahili: Mmiliki hawezi kukataa meno ya nyama.
